label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits input only on "\n" and never strips a trailing "\r", so it cannot handle CRLF line endings (the default for Windows-based export tools). With CRLF input, the header line ends up as e.g. "date,amount,description\r", so after splitting on "," the last header column becomes "description\r" instead of "description". That fails the `REQUIRED_COLUMNS` check in `assertShape`, which always throws `errors.rowShape` for row index 0 → reported as "row 1" — matching exactly what's described, regardless of the actual file contents. Each data row would have the same trailing "\r" issue on its last field too.

Since finance switched to a new Windows accounting export tool, it's very likely now producing CRLF line endings, while the parser was only ever tested/working with LF. The fix should normalize line endings (e.g. strip trailing "\r" per line, or split on /\r?\n/) in `parseStatement`.

Each data row would have the same trailing "\r" issue on its last field too.

Since finance switched to a new Windows accounting export tool, it's very likely now producing CRLF line endings, while the parser was only ever tested/working with LF. The fix should normalize line endings (e.g. strip trailing "\r" per line, or split on /\r?\n/) in `parseStatement`.
